seo.title: AI SQL assistant and local MCP server
seo.description: Explain, optimize and fix SQL with the AI provider you choose, and let MCP clients such as Claude Code use saved connections through a local MCP server.

header.title: AI assistant and MCP
header.lead: Explain or fix SQL with your preferred provider. Connect AI clients to saved connections through MCP (Model Context Protocol).

sections.title: Choose your AI provider
paragraphs: Supported providers: {aiProviders}. Use an API key, an existing account or a local model, depending on the provider. Requests go directly to your provider; TablePro runs no AI service. The feature is free, but provider charges may apply.

Messages include schema context and the query in the editor. Result rows are excluded unless enabled in <ui>Settings > AI</ui>. Set a connection's AI policy to Never to block both the assistant and MCP clients.

sections.title: Review, explain, optimize and fix
paragraphs: Review a statement, explain it or request an optimization. Fix with AI is available when a query fails. These actions send relevant schema and SQL without running the statement. <ui>Apply to Editor</ui> requires confirmation.
Inline suggestions are off by default. Add connection-specific AI Rules to provide instructions with each message; they are model instructions, not enforced database permissions.

sections.title: Chat modes and Agent mode
paragraphs: Ask is the default chat mode: it reads schema and runs no statements. Edit can run queries; Agent can also propose destructive statements. At the default {macSafeModeDefault} level, Edit and Agent writes can run without approval. Alert and stricter levels confirm writes; Read-Only refuses them. Destructive statements always require confirmation.

Full-window Agent mode is separate from the chat's Agent option. It keeps the connection at Alert or stricter, so writes wait for Run. Turning that mode off removes its minimum level. Sessions remain on this Mac.

sections.title: Connect external AI clients
paragraphs: The built-in MCP server gives clients access through saved connections without exposing their passwords. It is off by default and listens only on {mcpHost}. Enable it yourself or let a configured client start it.
Clients can inspect schemas and use permitted query, object and administration tools. Calls are logged locally with statement digests; executed queries also appear in query history.

blocks.title: Connect a client
paragraphs: Find setup instructions for {mcpSetupClients} in Settings > Integrations. The bundled tablepro-mcp bridge also supports {mcpBridgeClients} and starts the app when needed. Raycast uses a separate pairing flow that requires approval.
For example, ask a client to find duplicate email addresses. It can inspect the schema, identify the column and run a permitted SELECT through your saved connection.

blocks.title: What a client may do
paragraphs: Every call passes each of these checks, and the strictest one wins.
points: Token scope: Read Only, Read & Write or Full Access, optionally restricted to named connections. The bridge uses Read & Write, which excludes destructive statements.
External Clients: Blocked, Read Only (default) or Read & Write per connection. Blocked connections are not listed.
Connection approval: ask every time, once per connection or never.
AI policy: a connection set to Never refuses MCP clients too.
Safe Mode: confirmation follows the connection's level. DROP and TRUNCATE require Full Access and approval every time. File access and server-side code execution statements are refused.

sections.title: Use external MCP tools
paragraphs: TablePro's assistant can also call an external MCP server over Streamable HTTP. HTTPS is required except for local servers. Choose which connections can use each server; every tool call requires a click. Server settings stay on this Mac.

sections.title: Automation
paragraphs: AppleScript can connect, run a query and open a table, within the connection’s External Clients level and Safe Mode. tablepro:// links open a connection, a table or a query tab; a query in a link is filled in after you confirm and never runs by itself. Database URLs such as postgresql:// open as connections.

The tablepro shell command opens those URLs and files in the app; it does not run queries from the terminal. The official Raycast extension searches your connections, tables and query history, and runs queries through the paired app.

sections.title: Where your data goes
paragraphs: Prompts, schema and attachments go directly to your provider under its terms. Local models keep them on your machine when served locally. TablePro receives none of this content. External MCP clients handle accessed data under their own settings and terms.
When you add GitHub Copilot, its option to send telemetry to GitHub starts switched on; turn it off where you set Copilot up.

sections.title: Availability
paragraphs: AI, MCP and the automation tools on this page are currently available on Mac only.

limits: Cursor cannot call TablePro’s tools, so with Cursor as the provider, Edit and Agent run no queries. Local models call tools only if the model supports it.
Claude Agent uses your Claude Code login and reaches the schema through the MCP server, which has to be on. It depends on Claude Code and can break with a Claude Code release.
The MCP server listens on {mcpHost} only. Reaching it from another machine means forwarding the port yourself, and owning what that exposes.
The Mac app has no Shortcuts actions; automate it with AppleScript, links or the MCP server.
Agent sessions and outside MCP servers stay on the Mac where you set them up and do not sync.
